fomc-2026-09.standing: The rate-setting committee of the US central bank, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight federal funds rate. It anchors the dollar, sets the floor under borrowing costs worldwide, and every other major economy prices off it.
fomc-2026-09.recent: August consumer prices rose 0.4% as the Houthi capture of Yemen's port of Mocha pushed oil to $105, leaving the committee facing a supply shock and a payroll surge at once. Warsh has to decide whether an import-driven price rise is worth tightening into, and the 30-year mortgage at 6.71% is what that answer reaches.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate, the rate paid on reserves held at the Bank. Its decisions set UK mortgage and savings rates, and sterling moves with them.
boe-2026-09.recent: Andrew Bailey arrives at this meeting having warned the G20 that AI threatens a global economic downturn, a growth alarm from the governor who chairs the committee. It meets with oil at $105 after attacks on shipping, a cost paid in pounds at the pump, and the vote settles which of those two risks the committee weighs heavier.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions move the yen, the cost of Japan's vast government debt, and the global carry trade funded by cheap yen.
boj-2026-09.recent: The yen's slide past 160 per dollar has pushed Tokyo to weigh steering the currency with pension money, a 2014 playbook, rather than leaving its defence to the Bank of Japan's rate. With oil at $105 swelling the fuel bill of an import-dependent economy, this meeting settles whether the policy rate joins that defence.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The UK's monthly consumer price index, published by the Office for National Statistics. It is the measure the Bank of England's 2% target is written against, and it sets the uprating of pensions, benefits and index-linked gilts.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The September reading is the one the uprating formula reaches back to, so it fixes next April's pension and benefit rises rather than merely describing a month. It lands after a run of releases elsewhere in which energy costs did the work — petrol drove the sharp US increase in August — leaving the committee to separate a fuel pass-through from the domestic services prices it can actually reach.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the twelve-member body that sets the US federal funds rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. It is the reference price for dollar credit worldwide, and borrowing costs from mortgages to emerging-market debt reprice against it.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee arrives at this one arguing about a supply shock it cannot reach: oil at $105 after Houthi forces captured Yemen's port of Mocha, feeding an August CPI print of 0.4%, while a payroll surge removed the labour-market slack that would justify looking through it. Warsh has flagged the trap — imported inflation transmitted through the dollar, with emerging-market debt on the other side.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's rate-setting council, which meets about every six weeks to set the deposit rate for the countries that share the euro. Its decisions reach mortgages, business loans and government borrowing across the bloc.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Attacks on tankers have pushed Brent to $105, and the ECB has to decide whether an energy shock it cannot reach is now spreading into wider prices strongly enough to justify more hikes. Deutsche Bank has already raised its ECB peak to 2.75%. This meeting tests whether Frankfurt treats fuel as a passing cost or a lasting one.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set Japan's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, government bond yields and the carry trades that borrow in yen to invest abroad.
boj-2026-10.recent: The yen slid past 160 per dollar, and Tokyo is now weighing Japan's 2014 playbook: steering the currency through pension money rather than the policy rate. This meeting settles whether the Bank of Japan leaves the yen's defence to that channel or takes part of the job back with its own rate.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions feed straight into UK mortgage and savings rates, and sterling trades on every one.
boe-2026-11.recent: Andrew Bailey warned the G20 that AI risks a global downturn, and since then Brent has jumped to $105 on attacks on tankers, raising the fuel bill paid in pounds. This meeting sets that growth worry against an oil price driven by attacks at sea, which no rate decision lowers, and settles which of the two the committee answers first.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the twelve-member body that sets the US federal funds rate eight times a year. The rate it chooses is the reference price for dollar credit worldwide, and borrowing costs from mortgages to emerging-market debt reprice against it.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The committee arrives at this meeting arguing about a supply shock it cannot reach: Houthi fighters captured Yemen's port of Mocha, oil jumped to $105, and August consumer prices rose 0.4%. A payroll surge has moved hike odds to two-in-three, and Warsh faces the trap of tightening into imported inflation while the 30-year mortgage rate sits at 6.71%.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of heads of state and government from the world's twenty largest economies, plus the EU and African Union. It has no treaty powers and decides by consensus, so its output is a communiqué whose wording each member must accept.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US presidency has spent the run-up trying to rally the bloc against China's trade surplus while keeping Russia at the table — Siluanov's return to the finance track drew a European boycott of the family photo. Andrew Bailey used the same forum to warn that AI could cause a global downturn. What December settles is whether a coalition split over Moscow can agree on any text at all.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council meets eight times a year to set interest rates for every country that uses the euro. Its rates feed into mortgages, business loans and government borrowing from Lisbon to Helsinki.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Brent's jump to $105 after attacks on shipping in the Iran war has made this an energy decision for the ECB. The question is whether dearer fuel is feeding into wages and wider prices, the second-round effect that turns a price spike into a case for higher rates. Deutsche Bank has already raised its call for the ECB's peak rate to 2.75%.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions pass quickly into British mortgages, many of them on short fixed terms, and into the pound.
boe-2026-12.recent: Andrew Bailey told the G20 that AI could cause a global economic downturn, putting a growth risk on the record. Brent has since jumped to $105 on attacks on shipping, raising the fuel bill paid in pounds. The decision settles which the Bank treats as the larger threat: the slowdown its governor named, or an oil price it cannot reach.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's Policy Board, which meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions move the yen, Japanese government bond yields and the global carry trades funded in cheap yen.
boj-2026-12.recent: The yen fell past 160 per dollar, and so far Tokyo's response has come from outside the Bank of Japan: Japan is weighing whether to use pension money to steer the currency, echoing a 2014 playbook. This decision settles whether defending the yen stays with that workaround or reaches the policy rate itself.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-09-16.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly tally of receipts at US retail and food-service businesses, published about two weeks after the month it covers. Consumer spending drives most of the American economy, so the print moves rate expectations.
